### F1. `fetch config init` writes the TOML template into a `.yaml` path

- **Failure:** The user runs `fetch config init` with `--config fetch.yaml`. The command writes TOML into the file and reports success. Every later command then rejects that config with exit `2`.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — `maintainer fetch --config p1/new.yaml config init` printed `wrote p1/new.yaml`, exit 0. Then `config validate` printed `parse YAML fetch config` and exited `2`.
- **Fix:** `fetch config init` must write a config that loads under the format of its file extension, or refuse that path.

### F2. The implicit root fails in a working directory reached through a symlink

- **Failure:** The user opens a workspace through a symlinked folder and runs `maintainer status`. The command exits 1 and blames a symlink root that the user never configured.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — with `ln -s real link`, `status --format=plain` in `real` exits 0, and in `link` it exits 1 with `symlink roots are not followed`. inspected — `internal/command/status/root.go:45` takes the logical `os.Getwd`, and `internal/service/workspace/scope.go:159` rejects it.
- **Fix:** A bare `status` in a symlinked working directory must scan the folder that the symlink names.

### F3. A sparse or partial checkout is invisible to the scan, so a rename re-clones it

- **Failure:** A tracked checkout has `extensions.worktreeConfig` from `git sparse-checkout set`, or `extensions.partialClone`, and go-git cannot open it. The scan then skips it without a message. After a rename on GitHub, the plan clones the repository again, and the new record drops the old path.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — in overlay scratch tests, `Inspect` refused `extensions.worktreeconfig true` after `git sparse-checkout set --cone docs`, and refused `extensions.partialclone origin`. For a renamed tracked checkout, the plan showed `move` without sparse checkout and `clone acme/new` with it. inspected — `internal/service/fetch/adopter.go:120` drops the error; `internal/service/fetch/planner.go:469` builds the record without the old path.
- **Fix:** Fetch must recognise each usable checkout of a tracked repository. A rename must move that checkout or report it, and never clone the repository a second time.

### F4. A pin that GitHub does not confirm stops the whole fetch run

- **Failure:** A `repos` pin names a repository that GitHub does not confirm, such as a deleted one. `fetch` prints no plan and stops with `cannot verify explicit checkout`. The guide makes a pin failure a conflict of that repository only.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — an overlay service test with a pin `acme/gone`, a resolver that answers `404 Not Found` and a discovered `acme/tool`: `Run` returned that error, stdout empty. inspected — `internal/service/fetch/service.go:466`, `docs/content/fetch.md:178`.
- **Fix:** A pin that GitHub does not confirm must be a conflict of its repository, and the rest of the plan must go on.

### F5. A month cached with the API calendar while open keeps it after it closes

- **Failure:** On the last run of a month, the lists lag behind the total, and the cache stores the API calendar. After the month closes, an equal total reuses that calendar for good. A review near midnight then stays on its account-zone day, and no warning names the month.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — an overlay test: Oct 31 23:00Z with `undated: {"2026-10": 1}`, then Nov 1 with that contribution as a review on Oct 20 and the same total. `go test -overlay … -run TestScratchLag` prints `closed: map[2026-10-01:1 2026-10-10:2] months fetched: [] warn: `. inspected — `contribution.go:146` reuses any calendar entry once `month.open` is false.
- **Fix:** A calendar taken while the month was open must not be reused after the month closes.

### F6. A refused triage on a malformed file drops the issue instead of keeping it stale

- **Failure:** The user saves an issue file with a broken frontmatter, then sets a label in the hub. The hub answers `412` and removes the issue from the index. A reload gives `404`, and **Reindex** does not bring the last good version back.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — a scratch overlay test wrote `---\nbroken: [\n` to `MAIN-1.md` and called `ix.Patch` with the old version. It logged `task present=false` after the `412` and after `ix.Scan`. inspected — `docs/content/service.md:125` promises that such a file keeps its last good version.
- **Fix:** A refused write on a file that no longer parses must keep the previous entry, flagged stale, as a scan does.

### F7. Rename detection in one checkout holds the whole `status` run for minutes

- **Failure:** One checkout has a large or slow diff. The `git diff --find-renames --numstat HEAD` of that row takes minutes, and the user waits for the whole snapshot.
- **Evidence:** inspected — `.github/self-control.md` "Follow-ups to file" records 4 minutes over 164 checkouts, 2.5 of them in that command. `internal/service/status/git.go:181` runs it on each row.
- **Fix:** A `status` run must finish in a time that one slow checkout does not dominate.

### F8. skill status calls the skill of a pseudo-version binary incompatible

- **Failure:** A binary built from an untagged commit reports a pseudo-version such as `v0.5.1-0.2026…-1848546abcde`. `skill status` marks its own bundled skill incompatible, exits `1` and advises `install --replace`, which changes nothing; `SKILL.md` says a pseudo-version means compatibility unknown.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — built with `-X main.version=v0.5.1-0.20261125120000-1848546abcde -X main.commit=1848546`, `skill status` printed "incompatible with this binary, same as this release" and exited `1`; `skill install --agent claude-code --replace` printed "already holds". inspected — `internal/skill/status.go:234` parses the pseudo-version as a prerelease, `skills/maintainer/SKILL.md:51`.
- **Fix:** A pseudo-version binary must report the compatibility of a copy as unknown, as the skill tells the agent.

### F9. The sidebar repository tree never retries a failed catalog request

- **Failure:** The shell's first catalog request fails, for example while the service restarts. The page recovers on Try again, but the sidebar shows no Repositories tree until a full reload.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — a scratch vitest renders `App` at `/tablo` with `/api/v0/catalog` failing until Try again; afterwards 3 catalog calls, the page notice gone, `tree present: false`. inspected — `web/src/app.tsx:94` never calls `retry`.
- **Fix:** The sidebar's repository tree must appear once the catalog loads again, without a page reload.

### F10. F on the full issue page opens a hidden filter menu

- **Failure:** With the full issue page open, F opens the Filter menu inside the hidden top bar. Then P and E do nothing, and the first Escape closes the invisible menu instead of returning to the list.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — a scratch vitest on `/inbox?task=ID`: after `f` one `.popover` exists, `p` opens no command bar, and after `Escape` the URL keeps `?task=`. inspected — `web/src/components/TaskFilters.tsx:261` ignores whether the filters are shown.
- **Fix:** F must open the filters only while they are visible, and the issue page's P, E and Escape must keep working.

### F11. Inbox group counts ignore the Status filter of the list

- **Failure:** The user filters the inbox by Status (To do) and groups by priority. Each group header counts the tasks of every column, so "High 4" heads one row, against the guide.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — a scratch vitest of `groupTasks` with facets over all columns and one To do task gave count 4, not 1. inspected — `internal/service/hub/query.go:136` builds facets before the `column` filter, `grouping.tsx:150` takes the facet count, `docs/content/service.md:141` says a group counts the selection.
- **Fix:** A group header in the inbox must count only the tasks that match every active filter, the Status filter included.

### F12. `state prune` ignores `--owner` and `--profile` and forgets records of other owners

- **Failure:** The user runs `fetch state prune --owner a`. The help of `--owner` says "others are left alone". The command still forgets the missing records of every owner.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — a state with missing paths for owners `a` and `b`, then `fetch --config p1/fetch.toml state prune --owner a`. It printed `pruned 2 record(s)`, exit 0, and 0 records stayed.
- **Fix:** `state prune` must either prune only the selected owners and profiles or refuse the selection flags.

### F13. `lookup` prints its calendar table to stderr, so stdout stays empty

- **Failure:** A user runs `maintainer github contribution lookup > week.txt` or pipes it to `grep`. The file or the pipe gets nothing, because the table is the only result.
- **Evidence:** inspected — `helper.go:308` prints the table with `cmd.PrintErrln`, and `lookup.go:62` calls it as the only output. `MAIN-131` defers this split as "finding 30", and no open issue holds it.
- **Fix:** The `lookup` table must reach stdout; the `suggest` table and the diagnostics stay on stderr.

### F14. Contribution commands take a token from a `.env` file in the working directory

- **Failure:** A checkout holds a `.env` with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and the shell exports no token. `lookup` and `suggest` then read the calendar of the owner of that token. The guides name only `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `--token`, and promise a failure without a token.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — `.env` with `GITHUB_TOKEN=scratch-not-a-token`, `snapshot 2013` behind a dead proxy requested `https://api.github.com/user`, exit 1; without `.env`, exit 2. inspected — `internal/config/tool.go:35`.
- **Fix:** The token must come only from the sources that the guides name, or the guides must name `.env` and its precedence.

### F15. The service loader accepts repos match ids that service.cue rejects

- **Failure:** A `service.toml` rule with `match = { id = -5 }` loads, the service starts, and the rule matches nothing, though the guide says a bad value stops the service. A rule `match = { id = 0, owner = "a", name = "b" }` works in the service but fails `cue vet`.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — an overlay test of `LoadService` returned no error for both files; `cue vet -c internal/config/service.cue` rejected both. inspected — `internal/config/service.go:201` treats any nonzero id as set, `internal/config/service.cue:64` requires `id: int & >0`, `docs/content/service.md:245`.
- **Fix:** The service loader and `service.cue` must accept and reject the same repository matches.

### F16. The `-vv` and `-vvv` levels print nothing beyond `-v`

- **Failure:** A user runs `fetch -vv` or `-vvv` to diagnose a run, as `--help` and `docs/content/fetch.md` offer. The output equals `-v`: only `Debugf` writes at the debug level, and nothing calls it.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — an overlay test ran one apply at verbosity 1, 2 and 3; stderr held the same six lines each time. inspected — `grep -rn Debugf` finds only `internal/service/fetch/reporter.go:257`; `internal/command/fetch/root.go:61` advertises `-vv, -vvv`.
- **Fix:** Each verbosity level that the help and the guide offer must add output. Otherwise they must offer only the levels that do.

### F17. An owner listed next to the wildcard in `include_owners` is silently dropped

- **Failure:** A user sets `include_owners = ["*", "stranger"]`, as the fetch guide advises listing owners outside member orgs explicitly. Discovery expands only to the user and member orgs, and the allowlist then drops `stranger`'s repositories without a diagnostic.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — overlay test `TestScratchWildcardWithExplicitOwner` with `Owners: []string{"*", "stranger"}` logs only `snapshot: me/a`; the `/users/stranger/repos` route is never requested. inspected — `discovery_rest.go:100` replaces the whole list when any entry is `*`.
- **Fix:** A list that mixes the wildcard with owners must either discover those owners too or be rejected with a message.

### F18. At 390 px the Filter menu opens 82 px past the left screen edge

- **Failure:** A user opens Filter on `/tablo` or `/status` in a 390 px window. The menu spans x=-82 to 198, so the search field, the icons and the start of each dimension name are cut off.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — on a scratch hub at 390 px, a click on `.filter-button` gave a `.popover` box of `-82..198`. inspected — `Popover.tsx:73` flips to `popover--end` without a check of the left room; `base.css:2864` sets 280 px.
- **Fix:** At 390 px the Filter menu must lie fully inside the viewport on every page.

### F19. Below 600 px several controls stay under the 44 px touch size

- **Failure:** In a 390 px window, the Priority and Estimate triggers and the breadcrumb back button are 28 px high. The view switch segments are 32×40 inside an 84 px frame, with a 20 px empty tail.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — headless Chrome at 390 px on the scratch hub: `.prop__button` measured `h=28`, `.issue-header__crumb--back` `h=28`, `.view-switch__item` `w=32 h=40`. inspected — `DESIGN.md` Layout states "touch targets are 44 px" below 600 px.
- **Fix:** Below 600 px each interactive control of the hub must offer a 44 px target, as `web/DESIGN.md` states.

### F20. `make go-dist-installer` empties the tracked `bin/install`

- **Failure:** The maintainer runs `make go-dist-installer` and loses the install script, because `godownloader` is not a tool of `tools/go.mod`.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — in a scratch copy, `make go-dist-installer` exited with `godownloader: command not found` and left a 0-byte `bin/install`.
- **Fix:** No target must overwrite `bin/install` with output of a tool that the repository does not install.

### F22. A scan obstruction conflict prints `/` as its repository name

- **Failure:** An unreadable directory in the workspace prints `✗ conflict   /`, and `plan: 1 repos total` omits that row, so the user reads a nameless repository.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — overlay test with `chmod 0` on `<root>/public/acme` rendered `✗ conflict   /` above `at <root>/public/acme`.
- **Fix:** A conflict without a repository identity must print its path or a scan label instead of an empty `owner/name`.

### F23. A refresh during a collection runs two more collections instead of one

- **Failure:** Each **Refresh** pressed during a status collection costs an extra Git pass over every checkout, and the page shows refreshing longer.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — a scratch test held the first `collect`, called `Refresh` five times, and logged `collections: 3` on three runs, against `checkouts.go:13` "coalesce into one more".
- **Fix:** Refresh requests during a collection must yield exactly one more collection.

### F24. Closing the issue page leaves a duplicate list entry in the history

- **Failure:** The comment at `task.ts:29` promises that Forward reopens the issue, but the close replaces that entry, so browser Back then shows the same list.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — scratch `openTask('x'); closeTask()` from `/inbox` grows `history.length` by 1 and ends on `/inbox` again.
- **Fix:** Closing the issue page must leave no history entry identical to the one before it, and the comment must state the behavior.

### F25. The ci guide omits the `web` job and its `web/**` trigger

- **Failure:** A reader of the guide does not learn that ci runs `make web-check` and checks that `web/dist` is tracked.
- **Evidence:** inspected — `.github/workflows/ci.yml:24` and `ci.yml:173` hold the trigger and the job; `README.md:5`, `:84` and `:91` omit both.
- **Fix:** The ci section of the workflows guide must name the `web/**` trigger and the frontend check.

### F26. Four component sizes in the styles differ from `web/DESIGN.md`

- **Failure:** The View menu, rail code slot, Repositories header and comment text differ from the contract, so each design check flags them again.
- **Evidence:** inspected — `base.css:1188`, `base.css:1721`, `base.css:316` and `base.css:2131` against `display-menu`, the "100 px code slot", `sidebar-section-header` and `typography.prose` in `web/DESIGN.md`.
- **Fix:** Each of these four sizes must be the same in the styles and in `web/DESIGN.md`.

### F27. The token file holds menu alphas and light colors that the contract lacks

- **Failure:** The maintainer cannot check `--bg-menu` (92 % and 94 % against 86 % and 90 %) or seven light command and menu colors against `web/DESIGN.md`.
- **Evidence:** inspected — `tokens.css:27`, `tokens.css:125` and `tokens.css:141-148` against `bg-menu`, `light-bg-menu` and the absent `light-separator-menu` and `light-bg-command-chip` keys.
- **Fix:** Each color value of `tokens.css`, in both themes, must have an equal token in `web/DESIGN.md`.

### F28. No test fails when the tag signature gate accepts an unverified tag

- **Failure:** The maintainer gets no test failure when a change to `signature` lets `cd` publish from a tag that GitHub does not verify.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — in a scratch copy, `if (!verification?.verified)` became `if (false)`, and `release.test.mjs` still passed 11 of 11.
- **Fix:** A test must fail when the signature gate accepts a lightweight tag or an unverified signature.

### F29. No test covers the overwrite refusal of `fetch config init`

- **Failure:** The maintainer gets no test signal when a change lets `fetch config init` overwrite an existing config without `--force`.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — an overlay that disables the check at `internal/command/fetch/config.go:32` passed `go test ./internal/command/fetch/`.
- **Fix:** A test must fail when `fetch config init` overwrites an existing file without `--force`.

### F30. `histogram` prints with `fmt.Printf` and bypasses the command writer

- **Failure:** The maintainer cannot test the `histogram` output through the command writer, so no test covers it now.
- **Evidence:** inspected — `internal/command/github/contribution/histogram.go:61` calls `fmt.Printf`, and `histogram_test.go` tests only `HistogramScope`.
- **Fix:** The `histogram` output must go through the writer of the command.

### F31. The Friday case of TestTruncateToWeek tests a Tuesday

- **Failure:** The maintainer reads a Friday case in `TestTruncateToWeek` that runs on 2022-07-05, a Tuesday, so Friday is untested.
- **Evidence:** inspected — `internal/pkg/time/time_test.go:33` names Friday and `internal/pkg/time/time_test.go:34` builds `time.Date(2022, 7, 5, …)`.
- **Fix:** The Friday case must use a Friday date.

### F32. No test covers a tracked filtered repository whose checkout is missing

- **Failure:** The rule that keeps an excluded repository from a re-clone can break silently, and the maintainer learns it only from a user report.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — overlay mutation `if filtered {` → `if false {` at `planner.go:456`; `go test ./internal/service/fetch/ ./internal/command/fetch/` passes.
- **Fix:** A test must fail when a tracked filtered repository with a missing checkout is planned as a clone.

### F33. No test covers the closing status line of the human plan

- **Failure:** The maintainer gets no signal when the human plan prints a wrong outcome, such as a green `applied` after failed actions.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — overlay mutations at `reporter.go:167`, `:172`, `:179`, `:182` and `:208` each left `go test ./internal/service/fetch/ ./internal/command/...` passing.
- **Fix:** Tests must fail when the `applied`, error, orphan, `no drift` or `update` line of the human plan changes.

### F35. No test fails when the hash recheck before the rename is removed

- **Failure:** The maintainer gets no signal if the recheck at `write.go:570` breaks, because the test named for that race asserts nothing.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — an overlay that removed the recheck at `write.go:570` left `go test ./internal/service/hub/... ./internal/service/web/...` green; `write_test.go:233` discards the error.
- **Fix:** A test must change the file between the first read and the recheck and expect a version mismatch.

### F36. No test covers the rollback when the skill swap fails

- **Failure:** The rollback that restores the previous copy of the skill after a failed swap can break without a failing test.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — with `internal/skill/install.go:134` overlaid as `return err`, `go test ./internal/skill/ ./internal/command/` passed.
- **Fix:** A test must fail when a failed swap leaves no copy of the skill in place.

### F37. No test covers the 202 and non-JSON answers of the API client

- **Failure:** The maintainer cannot change `parse` or `getTask` safely, since deleting either branch keeps all 121 web tests green.
- **Evidence:** reproduced — a scratch config swapped in `client.ts` without the `getTask` 202 line, then without the `malformed` throw: `npx vitest run` passed 121 of 121 both times.
- **Fix:** A test must fail when a 202 task answer or a non-JSON error body is not reported as an `ApiError`.

### F38. Model functions without a production caller are kept and tested

- **Failure:** The maintainer keeps and tests `fileSource.Store`, `HistogramByDate`, `HistogramByWeekday`, `OrderByFrequency`, `HeatMap.From` and `HeatMap.To`, which no command calls.
- **Evidence:** inspected — `grep -rn 'HistogramByWeekday\|OrderByFrequency\|fileSource) Store' internal` finds only their definitions and tests.
- **Fix:** The model package must hold only the functions that the commands use.

### F39. `LabelChips` and `sameQuery` are exported without a caller

- **Failure:** The maintainer reads and keeps two exported helpers that no page, component or test uses.
- **Evidence:** inspected — `grep -rnw "LabelChips\|sameQuery" web/src` finds only `Chip.tsx:36` and `query.ts:68`.
- **Fix:** Every exported helper of the hub must have a caller.

### F40. Eight selector classes match no element that the hub renders

- **Failure:** The maintainer reads and keeps 12 dead rules when he changes the shell, the menus or the glyphs.
- **Evidence:** inspected — `git grep` outside tests finds no `activity__count`, `button--secondary`, `inbox-row__flag`, `menu-footer`, `menu-item__chevron`, `sidebar__items--nested`, `topbar__note`; `Glyphs.tsx:91` emits `glyph--priority-urgent`, not `glyph--urgent`.
- **Fix:** Each selector class in the styles must match an element that a component renders.

### F41. The divergence predicate of a checkout is written twice

- **Failure:** The maintainer must keep the status regex of the group and of the status tone in step for each new Git status word.
- **Evidence:** inspected — `model.ts:80` and `index.tsx:406` repeat `/ahead|behind|diverged|unborn/` with the same ahead and behind checks.
- **Fix:** One function must decide whether a checkout is ahead, behind or diverged.

### F42. The system theme block repeats the light theme block line by line

- **Failure:** The maintainer writes each light token change twice, in `tokens.css:112` and in `tokens.css:170`.
- **Evidence:** inspected — `diff` of `tokens.css` lines 113-167 and 172-226, with the indentation removed, reports no difference.
- **Fix:** Each light token value must be written in one place for the light and the system themes.
